circulation-cells.def: Large loops of rising and sinking air in each hemisphere: the Hadley cell (equator to about 30°), the Ferrel cell (about 30° to 60°) and the polar cell (about 60° to the pole). Air rises near the equator and 60° (wet) and sinks near 30° and the poles (dry).

coriolis.def: The deflection of moving air or water caused by Earth's rotation: to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.

prevailing-winds.def: The steady surface winds of each latitude band: the trade winds (0° to 30°, from the east toward the equator), the westerlies (30° to 60°, from the west) and the polar easterlies (60° to 90°, from the east).
